sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Employer of Record and Cross-Border Contractor Payroll

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (2012)
Cross-Strait Tax Arrangement on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: China: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended); PBOC/SAMR Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); PBOC/SAMR Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data (effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the PRC (2023 revision). Taiwan: Money Laundering Control Act and its Enforcement Rules; Counter-Terrorism Financing Act; Company Act; Employment Services Act; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; MOEA Company Registration Regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., SAMR in mainland China or MOEA in Taiwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at the origin notary; then apply either (i) Hague Apostille with the origin state's designated Competent Authority if the destination is a Hague Apostille Convention Contracting Party, or (ii) Consular Legalization through the destination state's embassy/consulate, or for Taiwan through the authorized Taiwan representative office, if the destination is a non-Hague jurisdiction. The Apostille and Consular Legalization paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or tax authority maintaining the corporate shareholder's active status record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certified copy; then use either Hague Apostille by the competent authority if the destination accepts apostilles, or full Consular Legalization by the destination's consular/representative office if the destination is a non-Hague state. No subsequent chaining of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for the incorporation of the JV and for UBO representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of each corporate shareholder, certified by the company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the board resolution under corporate seal; notarize the extract; then process exclusively through Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague destinations such as Taiwan, through consular/representative office legalization in accordance with the destination's entry requirements. The two methods are parallel alternatives, never a sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles (Charter) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registering authority or registered corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a certified true copy from the registry; notarize if required; then apply for either Hague Apostille certification or, where the destination jurisdiction is not a signatory, Consular Legalization through the destination's diplomatic/consular agent. Apostille and consular legalization shall not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each corporate shareholder and JV funding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The relationship bank of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the bank officer sign the reference letter before a notary; the notarized original is then either apostilled by the competent authority for Hague member destinations or legalized by the destination consulate/representative office for non-Hague destinations. These paths are exclusive alternatives and must not be applied in tandem.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner and the designated AML compliance officer, acknowledged before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the signed UBO declaration; then deliver through either Hague Apostille for Contracting States or Consular Legalization for non-Apostille destinations (including Taiwan-based acceptance where the Taiwanese office applies its applicable procedures). Apostille and consular legalization are independent options and cannot be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every corporate shareholder, director, officer, UBO, JV counterparty, intended EOR client, and staffing-agent counterparty must be screened before incorporation against OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU and HM Treasury sanctions, China's PBOC/SAFE AML watchlists and MOFCOM Unreliable Entity List, and Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission/FIU sanctioned-persons and Money Laundering Control Act databases. PEPs (domestic and foreign), family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval. Continuous adverse-media and negative-news screening is required for 24 months after formation, with audit-trail preservation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval System of the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (accessible through the One-Stop Company Registration Portal at gcis.nat.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English or romanized trade name may be filed as a secondary alias but does not create a separate legal name. The four-tier naming convention requires (i) a distinctive Chinese trade name, (ii) a business-scope descriptor tied to the EOR/staffing business, (iii) an organizational-type suffix such as Co., Ltd., and (iv) a distinguishing geographical or corporate identifier if needed to avoid identical or confusingly similar names. Romanization should follow the applicant's established commercial transliteration and must match the name used on contracts, bank mandates and the corporate chop.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If MOEA rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a written reasoned disposition. Within 30 days of service, the applicant or counsel must file a formal administrative appeal via the MOEA online portal, attaching a comparison matrix of identical/similar registered names, evidence of prior trademark or business-name use, and one alternative name. MOEA decides the appeal within three months. If denied, the applicant may commence administrative litigation in the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months. A pending name pre-approval may be extended once for up to 180 additional days by applying online before expiry and paying the statutory extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A mailbox-only virtual office is rejected for this industry. Taiwan's National Taxation Administration and municipal Labour Affairs Bureau require an actual physical business address where payroll records, employment contracts, uniform invoices, and AML/CFT files are maintained. A full-service serviced office with a physical suite, staffed reception, and a lawful sublease may be tolerable for company registration, but the Employment Services Act licence review and the JV bank's on-site compliance visit will normally require proof

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (as amended), particularly Articles 1, 2, 4-8 (incorporation), 128-135 (subscription), 156 (share capital), 192 (directors), 208 (managing director), 216-228 (auditors and statutory books), and Articles 387-389 (registration). Also apply the Investment Commission Regulations, the Statute for Investment by Foreign Investors, and the Foreign Investment Approval Guidelines under the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, operating through the Company Registration One-Stop Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Company Charter)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited company. The incorporators must however declare a reasonable issued capital amount, and the full subscribed capital must be deposited in a dedicated bank account in the company's name. A capital verification certificate issued by the bank must accompany the registration application. There is no blocked escrow account rule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Company shall issue and subscribe 1,000,000 ordinary shares at a par value of NT$10 per share, for an aggregate initial issued share capital of NT$10,000,000. The subscription shall be taken by the founding shareholders in the proportions set forth in the Joint Venture Agreement, and every subscriber shall pay the full subscription amount in cash into a dedicated share capital collection account maintained in Taiwan. The Chairperson of the Board is directed to provide the completed capital verification certificate to the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, together with the bank confirmation evidencing deposit.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson and the Company Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to open, operate, and maintain the Company’s primary corporate bank account at a licensed commercial bank in Taiwan. The authorized signatories shall consist of any two Directors whose specimen signatures are lodged with the bank, and such authorization shall remain in effect until rescinded by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation, which shall serve as the statutory seat for service of process, maintenance of statutory books, and official communication with regulatory authorities. The Chairperson is authorized to execute the lease, consent to use of address, and all documents required for the filing of the registered office with the Department of Commerce.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following statutory officers be and are hereby appointed: [Name] as Chairperson of the Board, [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as the Secretary, and [Name] as the Statutory Auditor, if required under Article 216 of the Taiwan Company Act. Each officer shall assume the fiduciary duties and statutory responsibilities imposed by Taiwanese law, including maintaining the shareholders’ register, preparing financial statements, and ensuring timely filing of annual returns.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Board delegates to the officers full authority to execute all registration instruments, to obtain the incorporation certificate, to arrange for tax and business license registration, and to take all ancillary actions necessary to complete the incorporation and commence lawful operations, subject to the shareholders and the Ministry of Economic Affairs approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the Investment Application Form through the MOEA Investment Commission's online portal. The application must be accompanied by the proposed Articles of Incorporation of the Taiwan joint venture, the Joint Venture Agreement, proof of identity or incorporation of each foreign corporate shareholder, a bank reference letter, and a business plan describing the EOR/global staffing services. All non-Chinese documents must be apostilled or notarized and translated into traditional Chinese by a certified translator, if required. After the applicant files the form, the Commission may request clarification or additional evidence. The applicant should respond to any clarification notice within fifteen calendar days to avoid rejection. Approval is subject to scrutiny of the foreign ownership ratio, national security concerns, and compliance with the Investment Regulations.
required_dossiers: Investment Application Form
Draft Articles of Incorporation for Taiwan JV
Joint Venture Agreement
Foreign investor's certificate of incorporation
Foreign investor's audited financial statements (latest year)
Passport or ID copies of directors and shareholders
Bank reference letter
Business plan for EOR/global staffing services
Power of attorney appointing a local agent
Notarized translations of all non-Chinese documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant must submit explanations and supplementary materials within 15 calendar days. If the application is formally denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days after notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Bank Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA via the Company and Business One-Stop Service, and a licensed commercial bank in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining foreign investment approval, apply for company name and business scope pre-approval using MOEA's Company and Business One-Stop Service portal, reserving the company's English and Mandarin names. With the pre-approval certificate, open a temporary share capital deposit account in the name of the future Taiwan company at a licensed bank. Each subscriber must remit the cash subscription amount from an outside account; bank remittance records plus the deposit certificate serve as capital verification. The bank will issue a capital verification certificate confirming that the funds have been deposited for the benefit of the company and are not withdrawn without the permission of the registrar. This certificate is a mandatory annex to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment approval certificate
Company name pre-approval application
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription schedule signed by shareholders
Passport or ID of the person opening the account
Bank deposit remittance records from subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit due to identification issues, rectify the signatory documents and re-submit to the same bank or choose another licensed bank. If MOEA rejects the name reservation, propose up to three alternative names and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Approval of Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) — One-Stop Business Registration Service (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application online to MOEA, attaching the pre-approval certificate, capital verification certificate, bank deposit certificate, articles of incorporation signed by all shareholders, the list of directors and statutory auditor with consents, the registered office location consent, and the foreign investment approval letter. The registrar will review the name, capital, corporate governance structure, and compliance with the Taiwan Company Act. Upon successful review, the company will receive its incorporation certificate and a unified business tax number. The company must then affix its company seal and directors' seal to all registration instruments. The registration fee must be paid electronically at the time of submission. If any document is missing, the registrar will suspend the application and require correction.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Company name pre-approval certificate
Capital verification certificate from bank
Foreign investment approval letter
List of directors and supervisors with consent forms
Registered office location consent (lease or ownership certificate)
Application for approval of company seals
Payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA returns the application for correction, the applicant has 15 calendar days to cure all deficiencies. If the matter is suspended because of a company name dispute, the company may submit a revised name application. If denied, the applicant may appeal under Article 17 of the Company Act within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (regional tax office), Ministry of Labor – Workforce Development Agency, and local municipal labor authority (e.g., Taipei City Department of Labor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the incorporation certificate, the company must file for business tax (business identity number) registration with the regional National Taxation Bureau, prepare the uniform invoice purchase certificate, and register for labor insurance, health insurance, and pension schemes for every employee or subcontractor. Because the company will operate as a Global Employer of Record and staffing agency, it must apply for a Private Employment Services Agency License from the Ministry of Labor. The application must include the incorporation certificate, the unified business tax registration, the responsible person's criminal record certificate from the police, the employment services operating plan, and the fit-and-proper declaration. The Company must also comply with the electronic records and privacy obligations under the Personal Data Protection Act when processing payroll data. Failure to obtain the license bars the agency from arranging employment and recruitment activities.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate
Unified business tax registration letter
Application form for private employment services agency license
Certificate of no criminal record for the responsible person
Employment services operations plan
Sample EOR services agreement and payroll outsourcing contract
Proof of office space and compliance with workplace safety
Consent to share employee data under the Personal Data Protection Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employment agency license application is deficient, the authority will issue an order to supplement; the applicant must cure within 15 days. If the license is refused, the applicant may request a review by the Ministry of Labor or file administrative litigation before the Taipei High Administrative Court within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Labor, Workforce Development Agency, and the local municipal Department of Labor (for employment service licensing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Services Agency License (Private Employment Services Institution Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — ISIC 7810 is an administrative and digital staffing service; no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment under Article 4 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. No EIA registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no wastewater process lines, VOC emission sources, or hazardous waste generation. The company must nonetheless recycle discarded electronic equipment (e.g., servers, computers) under Article 6 of the Waste Disposal Act and comply with energy-saving standards for office buildings, if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial fire permits. For the office premises, the company must register fire safety equipment maintenance and file annual fire safety improvement declarations if the registered office exceeds 200 square meters or is in a mixed-use building under the Fire Services Act. It must also conduct occupational hazard assessments for computer-based tasks, provide ergonomic furniture, and maintain work safety documentation under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. No structural load inspection is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF), Taxation Agency, through the National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; online electronic portal: MOF e-Tax Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw) and the MOF Unified Invoice Platform (e-invoice.nat.gov.tw)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a taxable presence in Taiwan, the entity must first appoint a resident tax agent and register the profit-seeking enterprise with the National Taxation Bureau. The procedure is: (1) submit a foreign company registration certificate duly notarized at a Taiwan consulate or by a local notary, together with the articles of incorporation and a board resolution appointing the Taiwan tax agent; (2) complete the national enterprise registration application through the MOF e-Tax Portal; (3) obtain the Tax Identification Number (TIN/VAT ID), which functions as the single business tax number; (4) file the separate Business Tax registration application for VAT purposes before commencing taxable sales; (5) for foreign digital or cross-border service suppliers without a fixed place of business, register through the MOF online system specifically for foreign enterprises and appoint a tax representative to handle VAT filings and invoicing obligations; (6) receive the Tax Registration Certificate and Uniform Invoice registration approval. All submissions must use the statutory forms embedded in the online portal and require the TIN for subsequent monthly or quarterly VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for corporate entities. A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture incorporated in Taiwan is taxed as a resident profit-seeking enterprise at the entity level. Hybrid mismatch treatment is not elective; the Taiwan Income Tax Act contains general anti-avoidance rules that may deny unintended double-non-taxation, and there is no fiscal unity or consolidated filing election for indirect tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary registration threshold; any business engaging in taxable sales in Taiwan must register with the National Taxation Bureau before making taxable supplies. For foreign businesses selling B2C digital services to Taiwan residents, registration is mandatory once Taiwan-source digital service sales exceed NT$480,000 per half-year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every registered VAT business subject to Taiwan's Uniform Invoice Regulations must issue a Uniform Invoice for each taxable sale. Under the electronic invoicing mandate, qualifying businesses must issue cloud-based e-invoices and transmit them to the MOF e-Invoice Platform through the statutory Turnkey API within 48 hours of issuance. No real-time pre-approval exists, but anti-fraud validation is performed by MOF through the Unified Invoice number, QR Code, cloud invoice stamp, and mandatory transmission acknowledgement. Businesses failing to transmit must bear the risk of disallowance of input VAT and exposure to penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 8 of the Value-Added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, zero-rating applies to: (1) goods actually exported from Taiwan and released under customs control by the exporting registered business; (2) services rendered wholly outside Taiwan or rendered in Taiwan to a foreign enterprise for use outside Taiwan, provided the proceeds are received in foreign currency and the service is not treated as a Taiwan-source supply; (3) goods supplied to an export processing zone or duty-free bonded zone in compliance with the Zero-Rated Sales Regulations. The exporter must prove through documentation that the goods physically left Taiwan and that the consideration was repatriated through certified foreign exchange channels.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Foreign Exchange Deal Slip or Settlement Confirmation from a Taiwan authorized bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Articles 51 and 53 of the Value-Added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, if an export zero-rating claim is materially deficient or unsupported by the required customs and foreign exchange documentation, the National Taxation Bureau will retrospectively assess the VAT at 5% plus interest and impose a statutory penalty of up to five times the amount of underpaid tax. In cases of deliberate fraud, false invoice issuance, or forged export documentation, criminal tax evasion penalties may apply, and the five-year general assessment period extends to seven years for fraud. Claimed VAT refunds are clawed back in full, and the exporter is barred from future zero-rate treatment until compliant customs and remittance evidence is produced.

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Foreign Exchange Department
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed floating NTD exchange-rate regime with foreign exchange controls administered by the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan). Current-account flows, including cross-border payroll, contractor disbursements, trade settlement, and service remuneration, are generally freely convertible through authorized foreign-exchange banks, subject only to declaration thresholds. Capital-account flows are more guarded: inbound equity subscriptions require advance approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the bank must see the approval letter before crediting the capital escrow account. The NTD is not a fully deliverable offshore currency for pure third-party speculation; all corporate NTD conversions must be documented with a genuine trade, investment, or profit-remittance purpose. Export proceeds must be repatriated into Taiwan within ten days from collection, but can remain in a Foreign Currency Deposit Unit account without mandatory NTD conversion, so the effective surrender ratio is zero on FCDU-deposited receipts. Profit remittances by a foreign shareholder are permitted once the JV's annual accounts are audited, tax returns filed, and no outstanding Central Bank declaration violation is pending. In practice, the regime is current-account liberalized and capital-account guarded, with the licensed Taiwan bank acting as the single clearing node for every inbound and outbound transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected and repatriated into Taiwan within ten (10) days from the date of collection. The exporter may either convert the full 100% into NTD with an authorized foreign-exchange bank or deposit the proceeds into a Foreign Currency Deposit Unit (FCDU) account. The mandatory NTD surrender ratio is zero per cent for proceeds placed in the FCDU account before the deadline; however, repatriation into Taiwan and the lodgment of the export collection record with the bank/customs framework remain absolute statutory requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and NTD/FCY Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Mega International Commercial Bank Co., Ltd.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with FCDU module
Payroll Disbursement Account and Cross-Border FX Settlement Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Unit (FCDU) Account for export proceeds and hedging

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal viability as a primary treasury or clearing rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise do not hold an authorized foreign-exchange bank license in Taiwan and are barred from opening a domestic NTD corporate clearing account or from executing the statutory foreign-exchange declaration on behalf of the JV. They may be used only as a supplementary payout API for non-Taiwan contractor remuneration after the source funds have first cleared through a licensed Taiwan bank; the EMI must not be named as the beneficiary bank on the capital escrow or tax-related settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is mandatory for the statutory responsible person or a locally appointed manager with a notarized power of attorney at the initial account activation and capital escrow opening. Pure remote/offshore consular proxy opening is generally not accepted by Bank of Taiwan, Mega, or CTBC for a foreign-invested trading/procurement JV; a responsible person may authorize a Taiwan resident manager to attend, but the bank reserves the right to require a one-time video interview with the ultimate foreign shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership opacity: Mainland China parent invests into a Taiwan JV, triggering deeper UBO and sanctions-adjacent scrutiny by the bank's AML committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized ownership chart to natural-person UBOs; audited financial statements of the Mainland parent for the last three years; PRC outbound investment (ODI) completion certificate; Taiwan Investment Commission inward investment approval letter; and a board resolution confirming that no sanctioned natural or legal person holds management or veto rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll-to-revenue artificiality: EOR payroll account receives client fees but deploys 70-90% of inflows to third-country contractors within 48 hours, causing a pass-through/round-tripping red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed global EOR master service agreements; headcount and contractor list; time and attendance records for each worker; proof of statutory registration as employer in each jurisdiction; monthly payroll ledger with mandatory tax/social-security deductions; and an accountant's letter explaining the gross-payroll/fee margin and remittance schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-value cross-border remittances to contractor beneficiaries in jurisdictions with weak AML oversight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete contractor KYC files containing passport, residence proof, independent-contractor agreement, and beneficial-ownership declaration; sanctions and adverse-media screening results; transaction-level remittance schedule mapping each SWIFT MT103 to an invoice; and an annual compliance audit report signed by a licensed CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payment APIs causing pooled settlement and masking the final beneficiaries of payroll.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficiary-level mapping between each Wise/EMI pay-out and the corresponding contractor KYC file; contractual commitment to cap aggregated omnibus settlement in Taiwan; monthly extraction of individual pay-out reports; and a signed treasury policy prohibiting bulk transfers to any shared pooled account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The JV's capital injection must be preceded by final inward investment approval from the Taiwan Investment Commission. The Mainland parent then sends a SWIFT MT103 wire in convertible foreign currency to the JV's capital escrow account at Bank of Taiwan, CTBC, or Mega, using a valid declaration purpose code for direct investment. The receiving bank will record the remittance, issue a foreign-exchange certificate, and allow NTD conversion only after the CPA's capital verification report has been filed with the authorities. Every wire should carry the JV's approved identification number in the beneficiary reference field to match the approval certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local NTD payroll should be run through the domestic clearing system from the operational payroll account, while foreign contractor payments and trade settlements are executed by SWIFT MT103 from an FCDU account, supported by the underlying service contract, invoice, and tax withholding certificate. For larger procurement or equipment-related trade, the JV may use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit or documentary collection through the same authorized FX bank, and overseas remittances must bear an approved FX purpose code reflecting the trade or service nature.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable NTD/USD forward contracts with licensed Taiwan FX banks for documented payroll, trade, and dividend exposure
FX swaps used to cover a simultaneous foreign-currency inflow and NTD outflow and to match the JV's funding cycle
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for JV long-term financing or capital-structure hedging

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts permitted only for offshore hedge counterparties when the NTD deliverable market is inaccessible, and always subject to Central Bank-approved trade-hedging documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Registration Confirmation of Responsible Persons and Major Shareholders (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Electronic System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation window from 1 January to 31 March of each calendar year; substantive changes (directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more) must be filed within 15 days of the change event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual confirmation or a 15-day change filing may be rectified under a MOEA order; continued non-compliance attracts administrative fines of NTD 10,000-50,000 under Company Act registration enforcement, and may be escalated to cancellation of the company registration, judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Withholding Statements for Employees, Directors and Cross-Border Contractors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed by 31 January of the following tax year; recipient copies must be delivered no later than 10 February.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or erroneous filing is subject to a fine of up to NTD 750,000 under Income Tax Act Article 114, plus collection of any under-withheld tax and interest; persistent non-compliance may result in compulsory execution and revocation of tax registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed each year from 1 May through 31 May following the calendar tax year; CPA-attested taxpayers may use the extended deadline to 30 June where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers, after notice, a 10% late-filing surcharge (minimum NTD 1,500) or, if the return remains unfiled, a 20% delinquency charge (minimum NTD 4,500) of the assessed tax; the tax authority may also assess tax upon information and initiate compulsory garnishment, ultimately leading to tax registration cancellation and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six statutory returns per year; each return must be filed by the 15th day of the month following the preceding two-month period (Jan-Feb, Mar-Apr, May-Jun, Jul-Aug, Sep-Oct, Nov-Dec).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed payment incurs a late-payment surcharge of 1% per 2 days up to 15% of the tax due; failure to file may lead to estimated assessment, seizure of bank accounts, suspension of business, and revocation of the business registration or VAT certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Adoption of Financial Statements (Company Act Article 20)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders and, through the minutes and any election changes, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) registration office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the AGM within the statutory window are liable to a fine of NTD 10,000-50,000; the competent authority may require the supervisors or, failing them, a court-appointed convener to call the meeting; chronic failures expose the JV to dissolution and strike-off remedies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Employment Services Institution Annual Statistical and Operating Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Labor or the authorized municipal labor affairs bureau (local Department of Labor)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 January of each calendar year for the preceding year's operations; also required at each license renewal interval established by the issuing labor authority.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is punishable by administrative warnings and fines of NTD 10,000-50,000 under the Employment Service Act; serious or repeated defaults give the licensing authority power to suspend or revoke the EOR/staffing license, which automatically terminates lawful operation of the licensed activity and may trigger winding-up of the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Company Act Article 20, the compulsory CPA audit trigger is expressed by balance-sheet capital: a Taiwan limited company whose paid-in capital at fiscal year-end exceeds NTD 30 million must file audited financial statements. The National Taxation Bureau applies an equivalent threshold-based independent audit requirement to profit-seeking enterprises whose turnover exceeds NTD 300 million, and Taiwan labor/employment supervisory practice treats a payroll headcount of 100 or more as a public-interest trigger requiring certified financial statements; any entity falling in these categories must engage a licensed Taiwan CPA to audit the statutory financial statements in accordance with the applicable accounting framework. Public companies, licensed financial institutions, and companies listed or traded on the TWSE/TPEx must be independently audited regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: TIFRS (IFRS as adopted by Taiwan) for public companies, financial institutions, and large corporate groups; for the subject private JV, Taiwan Accounting Standards or TIFRS for SMEs and local GAAP derived from the Commercial Accounting Act may be applied unless the enterprise exceeds audit thresholds, in which case full TIFRS is required. All audited financial statements must comply with the Company Act and Business Entity Accounting Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, every company must file responsible persons (directors, supervisors, managers) and major shareholders (10% or greater) with MOEA. The MOEA system requires an annual confirmation executed no later than 31 March in each year; any change, including any 10% threshold crossing, must be reported within 15 days of the date of change. Under Taiwan AML rules, the company must also maintain an internal beneficial-ownership register and complete any UBO update within 30 days of a 10% substantial owner change; the register must be made available to supervisors, AML authorities, and licensors on request.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% flat profit-seeking enterprise income tax; plus a 5% retained-earnings surtax on undistributed current-year surplus, making the effective corporate-layer burden 24% before shareholder-level dividend withholding tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday or patent-box regime applicable to a global EOR staffing agency; selected incentives include a 15% incremental research and development expenditure tax credit under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, investment tax credits for smart machinery and 5G hardware/software, and preferential treatment for qualifying free-trade-zone enterprises only where the statutory conditions and approved scope of operations are met

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Form No. 15), filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic tax filing and payment portal (taxweb.nat.gov.tw), together with the related-party transaction disclosure sheet and the enterprise income basic tax (AMT) return where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement declaration; no separate quarterly corporate income tax return, but a provisional income tax prepayment is due in September of the current tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, file between 1 May and 31 May of the following tax year; for an approved special fiscal year, file within five months after the close of the fiscal year; provisional tax prepayment for calendar-year entities is due by 30 September

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, Uniform Business Number, legal person registration, corporate registration history, business address, responsible person, bookkeeping system, and shareholder table
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Taiwan JV Uniform Business Number accurately; disclose all non-resident direct and indirect shareholders, especially the mainland China parent; if any non-resident shareholder owns 25% or more, identify the shareholding for double-tax-treaty, dividend WHT, CFC, and transfer-pricing screening; attach the register of directors and ultimate beneficial owner declarations to support the economic-substance file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and gross sales of the global EOR and cross-border contractor payroll service platform
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all platform service fees, placement fees, payroll-processing fees, and any service surcharges as gross revenue; income is Taiwan-source if the EOR services are performed from Taiwan or the payroll infrastructure is managed in Taiwan; do not net pass-through payroll unless the entity is strictly a disclosed agent of the overseas principal; non-resident customers do not change source character

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales returns, allowances, discounts, and rebates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct returns and discounts only with vouchers, debit notes, banking proofs, and board-approved adjustments; cross-border refunds to foreign clients require a valid foreign-exchange settlement and should be reconciled with prior-year declared gross revenue; erroneous netting with non-resident payables will trigger an audit adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, direct payroll, contractor compensation, and direct EOR delivery costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the EOR model, wages, statutory labor insurance, health insurance, and contractor payments are direct costs; local employee salaries must be supported by monthly withholding tax filings; salary payments to non-resident contractors for Taiwan-source services are subject to 20% non-resident WHT unless reduced by a treaty; payroll paid to foreign related parties must be priced at arm's length and supported by actual employment documentation in the jurisdiction where the contractor performs the work

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit and gross margin calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show separately the gross profit on EOR platform fees and any gross margin on intercompany subcontracting; if the entity is only a payroll payment agent with no employment risk or service risk, the tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement and allow only a commission-based net margin; any guarantee of contractor work or liability in the client contract supports gross revenue treatment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent, personnel recruiting, payroll software, legal fees, marketing, management fees, and general administrative costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct operating expenses only with valid Taiwanese documents, electronic invoices, or substantive foreign vouchers; fees paid to non-resident software licensors, foreign parent-affiliate management companies, or overseas head-office recharges are deductible only if WHT was withheld and remitted, the non-resident is the beneficial owner, and the amount satisfies the arm's length standard; failing to file Form-15 withholding disclosure for cross-border royalties or services will lead to disallowance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses: interest, dividends, royalties, foreign-exchange gains or losses, and other miscellaneous items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all interest paid to non-resident shareholders or related-party lenders, gross service royalties paid outbound, and foreign-exchange gains on cross-border payroll collections; Taiwan-source interest and royalty payments to non-residents are subject to statutory 20% WHT before remittance; treaty relief must be proven before the return is finalized; netting foreign-exchange gains against intercompany payables without real currency conversion will be disregarded

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, loss carryforward, alternative minimum tax, and related adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10-year loss carryforward only if the JV maintains complete accounting records and was audited or approved by the tax authority; loss from a foreign branch cannot offset Taiwan operating income; for AMT purposes, add back treaty-exempt income? no, AMT adds non-conventional tax-benefit income and offshore-specific investment income; non-resident-owned JV must also check Taiwan CFC rules for passive income retained in low-tax foreign affiliates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculation, tax credits, prepayments, withholding credits, and net tax due or refundable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute 20% tax on taxable income; deduct foreign tax credits only for taxes paid on foreign-source income that are included in the Taiwan taxable base; offset the September provisional prepayment and any domestic withholding credits; on the distribution or un-distributed surplus, separately compute the 5% retained-earnings surtax; if dividends were actually distributed to non-resident shareholders, declare the 21% dividend WHT and attach the corresponding withholding remittance statement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory attachments: related-party transaction disclosure form, transfer pricing report, CbC report, beneficiary declarations, and DTA relief forms
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the annual related-party transaction statement where aggregate related-party transactions exceed TWD 50 million; attach the local transfer pricing report where related-party revenue exceeds TWD 100 million; attach the parent-group joint filing and CbC notification where group revenue exceeds TWD 27 billion; for any dividend, interest, or royalty subject to treaty relief, include the non-resident's tax residency certificate, physical ownership statement, and the completed DTA application form; failure to attach any of these converts the return into an incomplete filing and suspends treaty benefits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a delinquency surcharge under Income Tax Act Article 108 of 2% of the tax payable for every two days of delay, capped at 10%; a supplementary notice and non-filing can raise the surcharge to 30%; late payment of assessed tax attracts daily late-payment interest based on the postal savings one-year time deposit rate; understatement of taxable income on an audited return is penalized under Income Tax Act Article 110 by fines up to three times the undercharged tax; fraudulent loopholes trigger Tax Collection Act Article 41 with imprisonment up to five years and a criminal fine up to TWD 10 million; unpaid tax balances exceeding TWD 1 million can subject the responsible director to a travel ban and blacklisting under Tax Collection Act Article 24 until the tax is secured or paid

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to a Taiwan non-resident corporate or individual shareholder; the 5% retained-earnings surtax applies at the corporate level before distribution, so the combined corporate tax and WHT burden on distributed profits is approximately 41% without treaty relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief is not automatic. The withholding payer must file the application for Chinese Taipei treaty benefit under the relevant double-tax agreement before remittance, attaching a tax residency certificate issued by the contracting state, a three-year beneficial-ownership declaration, audited shareholder register, board dividend resolution, and a statement that the non-resident does not carry on a trade or business in Taiwan through a permanent establishment; for mainland China residents, the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation provides a 5% dividend WHT where the beneficial owner holds 25% or more of the paid-in capital, 10% for other beneficial owners, and 7% for interest and 7% for royalties, subject to anti-avoidance limitation-on-benefits and beneficial-ownership recognition; if relief is denied at source, the non-resident may file a case for refund within five years from the statutory tax return filing date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory WHT on Taiwan-source royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 20%; full-tax treaties generally reduce the rate to 10% or provide a 0% rate for interest where the beneficial owner is the government of the treaty state; under the Cross-Strait Agreement, interest and royalties are each limited to 7%; for an EOR platform, common outbound royalty or interest items include payroll software licenses, global database subscriptions, cloud-service royalties, and intercompany shareholder loans, all of which require arm's length pricing and strict WHT settlement before remittance

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: TWD 100,000,000 in aggregate annual related-party transaction revenue triggers the mandatory local transfer pricing report and master file; related-party transaction disclosure is triggered at TWD 50,000,000; a group with consolidated revenue exceeding TWD 27,000,000,000 must additionally file a Country-by-Country Report and CbC notification
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan is not a zero-tax offshore jurisdiction and does not apply OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations as a series; instead, the tax authority relies on the general anti-avoidance rule in Tax Collection Act Article 12-1, the substance-over-form doctrine in income tax determination, and the economic-activity standards embedded in DTA permanent-establishment and beneficial-ownership rules; the JV must prove that its core income-generating activities, including employment contract execution, payroll computation, statutory labor insurance administration, contractor verification, legal compliance, and bank account management, are actually performed in Taiwan; a Taiwanese EOR entity that lacks employees, office premises, decision-making autonomy, risk assumption, and operating substance will be treated as a shell by the Taiwan National Taxation Administration, its related-party deductions will be recharacterized, and treaty benefits will be denied to the beneficial-owner test

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent tax evasion through shell payroll pass-through and offshore revenue diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan JV invoices fictitious or inflated EOR management fees to related foreign clients, records personal contractor salaries as deductible cost without payroll withholding, and diverts Taiwan-source platform fees to undisclosed offshore bank accounts of the mainland China parent; the annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return intentionally omits gross revenue from global contractor payroll settlements and management fee overcharges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Act Article 41: any taxpayer who evades tax by fraud or improper means is liable to imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to TWD 10 million; Income Tax Act Article 110 imposes an additional understatement penalty of up to three times the undercharged tax; the evaded tax, late-payment interest, and audit additions are all collected with civil enforcement priority over general creditors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false invoices, concealed offshore accounts, or false tax returns are jointly and severally liable with the company under Company Act Article 23 and Article 154 when the corporate form is abused; the National Taxation Administration may attach personal assets of directors under the tax collection procedure, apply to a court for a travel ban and blacklisting under Tax Collection Act Article 24 when unpaid tax exceeds TWD 1 million, and transfer the file to criminal prosecutors, who may impose up to five years imprisonment on the responsible director

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit non-resident withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The board files a distribution resolution but the JV wires the net amount directly to the mainland parent without deducting the 21% dividend WHT, pays foreign affiliate shareholder interest without 20% interest WHT, and licenses global EOR software from a related foreign affiliate with no 20% royalty WHT; the tax return falsely represents that no cross-border profit repatriation occurred while the bank records show remittance to offshore related parties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 114 requires the withholding agent to pay the under-withheld tax and subjects the withholding agent to a fine up to three times the amount of the tax not withheld; Article 88 imposes the withholding obligation on the payer at the time of payment; late remittance triggers interest and additional penalties; repeated intentional violation is criminalized under Tax Collection Act Article 42 for withholding agents who fail or fraudulently certify that withholding was performed
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who authorized the wire transfers is personally liable for the unpaid WHT as a responsible person of the withholding agent; the tax authority may seize the director's assets and freeze bank accounts; the director may be blacklisted and barred from leaving Taiwan until the outstanding WHT is secured; a responsible person who participates in false certificate issuance or incomplete withholding declarations can be prosecuted and sentenced to imprisonment for up to five years under the criminal articles of the Tax Collection Act

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation, non-existent local file documentation, and lack of substance in a treaty-claimed EOR platform
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV reports aggregate related-party service transactions of TWD 150 million, including management fees, software royalties, and contractor payroll recharges to the mainland parent, but prepares no transfer pricing report; the company claims 100% parent company guarantee on 30% annual service margin and books a zero-profit result by paying excessive foreign related-party service fees; the director signs a DTA treaty-relief declaration claiming benefits for a related affiliate that has no office, no personnel, no bank account, and no business operation in mainland China
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 43-1 authorizes the tax authority to recharacterize the transaction at arm's length and to increase taxable income by the artificially shifted amount; the transfer pricing assessment rules impose an additional penalty for failure to prepare, submit, or retain the local file and master file; Article 110 adds an understatement penalty up to three times the tax undercharged; a deliberate scheme with false documentation triggers Tax Collection Act Article 41 criminal prosecution and also invalidates the treaty claim, exposing the company to the full statutory 21% dividend or 20% royalty/interest WHT with interest and fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve and sign transfer-pricing documentation that is knowingly false are personally liable for the resulting civil tax debt under Company Act Article 23; the director may be ordered to restore diverted assets to the Taiwanese entity to satisfy tax arrears; Taiwan customs and tax authorities will blacklist the responsible person and issue a departure ban under Tax Collection Act Article 24; criminal proceedings may result in imprisonment up to five years and confiscation of personal property held in Taiwan, including offshore beneficial interests, for the sanctioned tax evasion and fraudulent treaty abuse
